config.title: Design Real-Time Dashboard

intro.title: Design Real-Time Dashboard
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a real-time dashboard that displays live data updates, such as stock prices or sensor readings, in a clean, responsive layout. You will learn how to use Angular's built-in HttpClient to fetch data from a mock API and how to bind this data to your template using interpolation and property binding. The core concept involves managing component state to handle dynamic data and updating the UI reactively as new information arrives. By the end, you'll have a functional dashboard that automatically refreshes with simulated real-time data, giving you hands-on experience with Angular components, services, and data binding.
intro.usecase: Real-time dashboards are essential in modern applications that require live data monitoring and decision-making. Developers build these for financial trading platforms showing live stock prices, operations centers tracking delivery fleets, or analytics tools displaying website traffic as it happens. In Angular, implementing such dashboards involves managing dynamic data streams, updating UI components efficiently, and providing responsive visualizations. Mastering this pattern prepares you for building critical monitoring interfaces across industries like finance, logistics, and IoT systems.

objectives: Construct a dashboard component with a responsive grid layout using Angular Material components
Initialize and bind real-time data streams to dashboard widgets using Angular services
Configure interactive controls that manipulate dashboard data display parameters
Implement data visualization components that render live metrics with automatic updates
Integrate multiple data sources and update dashboard elements simultaneously
Apply reactive programming patterns to handle asynchronous data flow in the dashboard
Control dashboard state and user interactions through Angular event binding

steps.title: Import Angular core modules and components
steps.instruction: Import Component, OnInit, and CommonModule from '@angular/core' and '@angular/common' respectively.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with the correct module paths. Component and OnInit come from '@angular/core', while CommonModule comes from '@angular/common'.
steps.seedCode: // Import Component, OnInit, and CommonModule here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular modules are imported, enabling component creation and common directives.
successCriteria: Component and OnInit are imported from '@angular/core', and CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some modules, but not all required ones. Make sure to import Component, OnInit, and CommonModule from their respective packages.

steps.title: Create the main DashboardComponent class
steps.instruction: Create the DashboardComponent class with the @Component decorator and an empty template.
steps.hint: Use the Component decorator from '@angular/core' and define a class named DashboardComponent with an empty template string.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component } from '@angular/core';

// Create the DashboardComponent class with @Component decorator and empty template
steps.expectedOutcome: The DashboardComponent class is defined with a basic Angular component structure.
successCriteria: DashboardComponent class is created with @Component decorator and empty template string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined the DashboardComponent class with the @Component decorator and an empty template string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DashboardComponent class isn't properly defined. Check that you've used the @Component decorator and created the class with an empty template.

steps.title: Define dashboard data interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'DashboardMetric' with properties: 'title' (string), 'value' (number), and 'trend' (string).
steps.hint: Create an interface using the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions.
steps.expectedOutcome: An interface named DashboardMetric with three typed properties will be created for type-safe dashboard data.
successCriteria: DashboardMetric interface is defined with title (string), value (number), and trend (string) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure all three properties (title, value, trend) are included with correct TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to use the 'interface' keyword with proper property types.

steps.title: Initialize dashboard metrics array
steps.instruction: Inside the DashboardComponent class, create a property named 'metrics' that is an array of DashboardMetric objects. Initialize it with at least two sample metric objects matching the DashboardMetric interface structure.
steps.hint: Define the property with type DashboardMetric[] and assign it an array containing objects with id, title, value, and unit properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a populated metrics array ready to display dashboard data in later steps.
successCriteria: The DashboardComponent class contains a 'metrics' property of type DashboardMetric[] initialized with at least two sample metric objects.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the metrics property, but it needs to be initialized with at least two sample metric objects matching the DashboardMetric interface.
steps.feedbackWrong: The metrics array property is not properly defined or initialized. Make sure to create a 'metrics' property with type DashboardMetric[] and initialize it with sample data.

steps.title: Implement OnInit lifecycle hook
steps.instruction: Make your DashboardComponent implement the OnInit interface and add the ngOnInit method to log a message when the component initializes.
steps.hint: First, import OnInit from '@angular/core'. Then, add 'implements OnInit' after the class name. Finally, define the ngOnInit method inside the class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will implement the OnInit interface and have an ngOnInit method that logs a message to the console.
successCriteria: DashboardComponent implements OnInit and has a defined ngOnInit method that logs a message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've imported OnInit, added 'implements OnInit' to the class, and defined the ngOnInit method with a console.log statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't properly implement the OnInit lifecycle hook. Check that you've imported OnInit, implemented the interface, and added the ngOnInit method.

steps.title: Create the main container structure
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a main div container with a dashboard header inside it.
steps.hint: Add a <div> element with a class like 'dashboard-container' and inside it, add an <h1> element with the text 'Real-Time Dashboard'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now contains a main container div with a dashboard header.
successCriteria: A <div> element exists in the template
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have both a container div and a header with the correct text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the required container structure. Try adding a div with a header inside.

steps.title: Add metrics display section
steps.instruction: In the DashboardComponent template, add a <section> element with a heading that says 'Dashboard Metrics'.
steps.hint: Add the section inside the template string, using HTML-like syntax with Angular's template syntax.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DashboardComponent template now contains a section element with a heading for metrics display.
successCriteria: The template includes a <section> element containing an <h2> element with the text 'Dashboard Metrics'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Implement ngFor loop for metrics
steps.instruction: In the template, add a *ngFor directive to iterate through the metrics array and display each metric's title, value, and unit.
steps.hint: Use *ngFor to loop over the metrics array and display each metric's properties using interpolation.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Looping through items
  • {{ item.name }}: {{ item.count }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will include a *ngFor directive that iterates through the metrics array and displays each metric's properties.
successCriteria: The template contains a *ngFor directive that loops over the metrics array and uses interpolation to display title, value, and unit for each metric.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the *ngFor directive, but make sure you're displaying all three properties (title, value, unit) for each metric using interpolation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The *ngFor directive is missing or incorrectly implemented. Check that you're iterating over the metrics array and displaying each metric's properties.

steps.title: Display metric data in cards
steps.instruction: Inside the template, create a div element for each metric card and bind the title, value, and unit properties from the metrics array.
steps.hint: Use Angular's interpolation syntax {{ }} to display the property values inside the card div.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying data in a template

{{ item.name }}

{{ item.value }} {{ item.unit }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain div elements that display the title, value, and unit for each metric in the metrics array.
successCriteria: Each metric card div displays the title, value, and unit properties using interpolation syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started displaying the metric data, but make sure each card shows all three properties: title, value, and unit using the correct interpolation syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The metric data isn't properly displayed. Check that you're using interpolation syntax {{ }} to bind the title, value, and unit properties from each metric object.

steps.title: Add CSS classes for styling
steps.instruction: Add the CSS class 'metric-card' to the div element inside your ngFor loop that displays each metric.
steps.hint: In Angular templates, you add CSS classes using the class attribute. Add class="metric-card" to the div that wraps each metric's content.
steps.analogousExample: User Details
steps.expectedOutcome: Each metric card will have the CSS class 'metric-card' applied, allowing for targeted styling in later steps.
successCriteria: The div element inside the ngFor loop has the class attribute with value 'metric-card'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added class="metric-card" to the div that wraps each metric's title and value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The metric cards don't have the required CSS class. Add class="metric-card" to the div element inside the ngFor loop.

steps.title: Add real-time update simulation
steps.instruction: In the DashboardComponent class, create a method named 'updateMetrics' that randomly updates the values of each metric in the metrics array.
steps.hint: You can use a forEach loop to iterate through the metrics array and modify each metric's value property with a random adjustment.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an updateMetrics method that can modify metric values when called.
successCriteria: The DashboardComponent class contains a method named updateMetrics that updates the value property of each metric in the metrics array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your method is named 'updateMetrics' and it modifies the value property of each metric in the metrics array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateMetrics method is not properly implemented. Check that you're correctly accessing and updating the metrics array values.

steps.title: Wire update method to component lifecycle
steps.instruction: Inside the ngOnInit method, call the updateMetrics method and set up an interval to call it every 3 seconds to simulate real-time updates.
steps.hint: Use setInterval to call updateMetrics periodically and store the interval ID in a variable. Remember to clear the interval when the component is destroyed.
steps.expectedOutcome: The dashboard metrics will automatically update every 3 seconds, simulating real-time data changes.
successCriteria: The ngOnInit method contains a call to updateMetrics and sets up a 3-second interval that calls updateMetrics periodically.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling updateMetrics both initially and within the interval. Also ensure the interval is set to 3000 milliseconds (3 seconds).
steps.feedbackWrong: The update method isn't properly connected to the lifecycle. Check that you're calling updateMetrics in ngOnInit and setting up an interval that calls it every 3 seconds.
